brief.description: FICTIONAL DEMONSTRATION. Vector Hatch Components is an invented B2B component supplier used only to evaluate an editable website builder. Its supplied demonstration range contains exactly three records: VHC-MP-01 Mounting Plate Concept, VHC-SB-02 Sensor Bracket Concept, and VHC-SC-03 Shaft Collar Concept. Material notes are illustrative aluminium or steel references, not material certificates. The site helps equipment buyers recognise the available component types, identify the matching product reference, and send a drawing or requirement for a discussion. Describe the proposed cooperation steps as: share intended use and drawings; clarify material and geometry requirements; review the proposed scope before any quotation. Do not state measured tolerances, production capacity, machine inventory, certifications, patents, customer names, prices, minimum order quantities, sample availability, lead times or shipping promises: none were supplied. No track record or factory ownership is verified. Use a product catalogue linked to the three real draft records and a native product detail template; do not repeat product cards as a second static list. Include Home, Components, How We Work and Contact, with native navigation and an inquiry CTA such as Discuss a component linking to Contact. Use the supplied components concept as an illustrative product-family image, never as proof of a particular SKU. The factory concept may illustrate a process section only if its caption clearly says AI-generated fictional factory illustration; omit it if that qualification cannot be retained. Put the visible statement Fictional demonstration — component and process illustrations on the site. Contact details, technical drawings, tolerance evidence, company registration, address and actual facilities are missing; leave them unclaimed and flag them for review. Do not invent an address, phone number or downloadable CAD file. Optimise page titles and descriptions for the actual supplied component types and buyer task; no search volume or ranking promises. The main conversion is a project discussion, not online payment or instant quotation.

brief.description: FICTIONAL DEMONSTRATION. Alder Bay Living is an invented home-living brand for a local editable-site rehearsal. Its supplied demonstration collection consists of three native product records: Fern Reading Chair ABL-FR-01, Cove Two-seat Sofa ABL-CS-02 and Pebble Side Table ABL-PT-03. The brand idea is considered furniture for quiet everyday spaces, expressed through a balance of softer seating and small supporting pieces. This is a design narrative, not a sustainability, durability or origin certification. The buyer is an independent home retailer, interior designer or small hospitality purchasing team in the US and Canada. Main action: Explore the collection, leading to the actual collection page; secondary action: Discuss your space, leading to Contact. Suggested pages are Home, Collection, Our Point of View and Contact, plus the native product-detail template for actual products. The homepage should feel like an editorial introduction: a supplied atmosphere reference, a concise brand viewpoint, one dynamic collection list and a route to a project conversation. The collection page must render only the actual three product records through a single editable dynamic list; do not repeat static cards with the same product names. Product descriptions are explicitly illustrative and carry no dimensions, material-performance testing, stock, price, warranty, delivery or production claims. Material references are concepts only and need confirmation. Reuse the supplied interior, chair and sofa images strictly as illustrative mood and category references; they are not verified photographs of these named products or completed customer projects. Any image caption and alternative text must preserve that distinction. Clearly show Fictional demonstration — furniture and interior references. No factory location, supply chain, certifications, sustainability claim, named designer, customer review, partnership or completed hotel project has been provided. No claims about FSC, recycled content, emissions or fire testing may be added. Missing facts are real product photography, specifications, material testing, ordering terms and company contact channels. Keep these unclaimed rather than guessing. SEO should describe the supplied collection and audience in natural English, with distinct titles and descriptions, not keyword stuffing or promises of AI recommendation or search rankings. All page layouts, product cards, original images and phone styling must remain editable native components.
